chapter: The levee club and the St. Louis scene
title: Cecil Scott's band at the Congo Roof Garden and radio
summary: Dance mentions Cecil Scott in New York. Thomas says that Cecil was a St. Louis drummer whose band played the Congo Roof Garden, broadcast nightly and did a WIL afternoon gig.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Yes, I see because he'd be playing with another band. Well, what we've got to link up now is after you'd worked for this place on the levee, where do you go from there?
That's what I'm wondering, too. Let me see.
Because we're getting up to, according to this book, you went to New York in '28 with Cecil Scott.
No, they got the wrong idea.
Because you're coming up to '28 by now.

Yeah but it's not the same Cecil Scott. They got the names mixed. Cecil Scott was a drummer and we worked in St. Louis. Tremendous organizer. Had a tremendous band we thought, you know. Worked at a place called The Congo Roof Garden.
How do you say it again?

On The Congo Roof Garden. No, Congo Roof Garden. What else? We sat up there with no hats on and burned the hell out of us, sweating like hell ... but we had -- thank you, Ken Stan, that's wonderful of you. We had Ken Ricks (?). We broadcast with Ken Ricks from maybe 12 o'clock at night until 4 in the morning. And I had some other gigs with a guy that liked my little trumpet playing and I had a little gig in the afternoon for WIL.
So now we're up to radio time now.
